After
loving the first game
, I moved on to the first sequel in the series, and am glad to see the disappointing sequel trend did not start with Warrior Within! Before I regale you with my complaints about this game, let me complain a bit about how hard this game is to actually access in the first place. So I played the first Prince of Persia through
SDLPoP
, an open-source port of the game, with a
lot
of fixes, accessibility options, and most importantly, compatibility. I had almost no problem setting it up on my Steam Deck and had a great time playing through the game. With the sequel, I though, "How bad can a DOS only game be to play?", well it turns out it's not the best.
So I went through the rigmarole of setting up RetroArch and DOSBox Pure and getting the game to run and all, which was a bit annoying in the first place, but lo-and-behold, I end up with the game of course not having the controls mapped properly (which is okay), but worse even, is that even after mapping all the buttons, the game flat out ignores my button presses at random times. Like legit the Prince chooses not to listen to my inputs, which would work if this game was super meta and wanted to make some sort of statement about us playing God in games, but I highly doubt that. I then tried to go about playing the Macintosh version, hoping that would fare better, but I couldn't even get that to run. I gave up on the idea of playing this on my Deck and settled for playing it on my laptop with regular DOSBox, which thankfully worked after a lot of tinkering. (Quick side note: ResetEra member
FluffyQuack
is working on a sort of
reverse-engineering project
to make this less frustrating.)
Another good title screen
Anyways, all that preamble out of the way, you can imagine my headspace after going through all of that. I was basically in a "Let's just get this over with" mood, which might have not helped the game's chances at winning me over.
The game starts off with a fully drawn & voiced cutscene, and you can tell a lot of that original PoP success went to the presentation. Whereas the original had no dialogue, this goes for regular-ish style for the time, which imo is basically the perfect summation of why this game misses what made the first so good. The simplicity of the original is what made it so good. You had a story that needed no dialogue (though it did have a text crawl in the beginning), you had extremely simple but distinctive pixel art, and most importantly, you have short & concise levels that each had a purpose.
Jaffars in the world do not appreciate how common their names are for Middle Eastern villains
After finishing the first game, I tried out the SNES version which had many of the same issues. It adds 8 new levels (all of which are decent-to-good), and "fixes up" the graphics and presentation. I found that to be a step down from the original game, which has such an iconic look and feel (that same feature that games like Pac-Man, Tetris or DOOM had), that was lost in the SNES version. Well, this game one-ups the SNES version because a lot of the levels here are plain frustrating.
The game controls pretty much the same as the first, so in terms of that there isn't too much to complain about (minus the jumping being borked slightly). The actual level & game design is what really brings the game down for me. Whereas the first was so intricately designed to where I almost always knew what to do or where to go, this one has so many obtuse puzzles, asks insane things of you, and throws "GOTCHA" moments at you every level. There were so many times where I accidentally locked myself out of being able to do something or go somewhere and had to kill myself and restart the level (or from a checkpoint).
On top of that, it also throws away one good part of the original, the combat. Every single encounter in the original had you sword-fighting one enemy, whereas here you fight floating heads, snakes, or aforementioned enemies, all of which are very frustrating to fight. All of this led to this game being the first one in the series I full-on cheated my way through. After looking it up, there's a bunch of cheats that made the experience smoother, and I am not ashamed to use them to power through the game.
When I think Persia, I think floating heads
This all reads very negatively, and to be honest the game probably is one of my least favourites in the series, but it does have some redeeming qualities. The main one, which is both a plus and a minus, is the crazy bonkers story that has you talking to a witch, fighting some sort of bird clan, riding a horse statue, killing clones of yourself in some sort of life-size Chess dreamscape sequence. All very bizarre, like something you'd find in some weird David Lynchian movie, none of which I can make sense of. The game's got a lot of these weird sequences and I appreciate the variety of environments you go through in the game. The art is pretty good too, though again, I prefer the simplistic art in the original.


I can't think of too much else off the top of my head. I was very disappointed by the game and am likely not to play it again. I know it's got its fans, and I'm sure I would've liked it more had I played it as a kid, but I'm okay leaving this in the past and not rewinding back to it. The only way I'd properly go through it again would be some sort of remake that fixes my issues with it.
What'd you think of the game? I'm off to my last unplayed PoP game, PoP3D! Wish me luck.

I almost feel obligated to try to defend POP2 a little bit. Aside from some rather gimmicky puzzles that feels a bit janky or obtuse (like the skeleton bridge fight or the entire final level), I think the level design is great and a notable step up from the first one. I really appreciate how much more open the levels are. If you end up dying in a level, chances are you can explore a different route which makes retrying more interesting.
I think the way the first cavern level is designed is pretty clever. You can head left and find a relatively short path to one exit if you're willing to take a chance on a big drop that you can't get back from. Or you can head right which leads to another exit which takes longer to reach but has a more straightforward path. At the end of the first path, you can see a health upgrade option that's inaccessible. Close to the second exit, you can take a detour which lets you take that potion, but it forces you back towards the first exit.
I like that type of design. You can go with either route through the level, but if you want the health upgrade, you have to take a more elaborate path that's a mix of the two.
There are many other levels I really appreciate. Like the sequence of jumps to get onto the horse statue that's really satisfying once you figure out how to follow the path. That's rather punishing as you have to restart the level if you mess up, but the level is very short so you don't have re-do much. And, in general, I think POP2 has much more interesting challenges in figuring out how to get from A to B in many rooms. Particularly when it figuring out how to grab the various health upgrades.
One common complaint about the game is its difficulty, and I think I agree it probably goes a bit too far. It would have been nice if it had a lower difficulty setting available. There's a lot of traps in the game that forces you to restart the previous checkpoint if you fall in them (through it is possible to figure out where many of them are by playing carefully and doing a small hop in many screens to see where the loose/flip tiles are). And, of course, the head and snake enemies are notoriously difficult to fight.
I personally really like the story direction of the game. And I'll give a shout out to the voice acting. There were games with good voice acting by that point, but voice acting was rare and the quality of it varied greatly. So it's nice to see an early example where the voice acting is great and fits the game perfectly.

Karachi: The port city continues to witness an unusual ordeal in the form of waves of seismic activity, as tremors were once again felt in eastern parts of Karachi late Wednesday night, bringing the total number of earthquakes since June 1 to an alarming 37. This marks the first time in the city’s recorded history that so many earthquakes have occurred in such a short span—just 12 days. According to the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD), the latest tremor was recorded at 1:44 AM in areas including Quaidabad and Malir. The earthquake measured 2.6 on the Richter scale with a shallow depth of 10 kilometers. The epicenter was located in the outskirts of Karachi. The residents reported feeling the tremor for a few seconds, prompting many to evacuate their homes in fear. Although the quake was of low intensity, it was strong enough to be felt in several parts of the city, including Gadap, DHA, Korangi, and Malir. The authorities have corroborated that no casualties or property damage have been reported so far. Nonetheless, the frequency and consistency of the tremors have raised ominous impression among the experts and residents alike. The seismologists noted that the recent quakes have ranged in magnitude from 1.8 to 3.6. While none of them have been strong enough to cause significant damage, the persistent tremors are unusual and are being closely monitored by geological agencies. On the other hand, the experts have stressed the public to remain calm but vigilant, advising residents not to spread rumors and to follow official guidelines in case of an emergency. The authorities are reportedly increasing surveillance and preparedness in vulnerable neighborhoods, while the emergency response units remain on alert in case of a stronger quake. Karachi, although not traditionally known for seismic instability, lies close enough to fault lines to be affected by minor tectonic shifts. The recent uptick in seismic activity has prompted calls for updated disaster management protocols and greater public awareness regarding earthquake preparedness.

The growing trend of encouraging educators to learn about how children’s brains work can offer reassurance, but it risks teachers’ autonomy and critical thinking, a new study warns.
Neuroscience is having a growing impact on the way teachers work. This is shown by the increasing number of professional development courses about the subject for those working in schools around the world.
The study warns this training does not always take account of the social context in which schools operate. If teachers are told biological information is more important than their pedagogical training and experience they could feel devalued, despite the possible positive influence of the training on their work.
Researchers say neuroscience can be a useful tool, but only when viewed critically and not shown as the superior or only way to teach. The courses they examined in Chile are often not regulated or inspected, and left to the rules of the market, so should be used in conjunction with the skills and socio-educational knowledge teachers have, rather than in isolation.
The study
, by Daniel Leyton and Lauren Stentiford, from the University of Exeter, is published in the journal Critical Studies in Education.
Dr Leyton said: “The professional value of teachers’ other skills is equally as important and should be respected. Neuroscience training which has information about learning styles, how the brain learns, and the sort of food children should eat to increase their capacity, for example, can be a useful addition and are well intentioned but care needs to be taken to ensure the teaching profession is not left devalued, and teachers keep bringing nuanced understanding of inequalities and injustices in schools.”
The study says neuroscience training can be empowering, but its increasing use in schools risks weakening teachers’ understanding of themselves and students and parents and the historical and social contexts in which schools operate.
Researchers interviewed 19 teachers and teacher educators in Chile. Those working in schools in that country work in an environment where they are often regularly observed or set targets, which puts pressure on them to experiment with tools such as neuroscience.
They also mapped CPD courses in neuroscience available for teachers in Chile run from 2007 to 2023 and examined neuroscience information on YouTube videos, podcasts, media interviews, academic journals and books.
Through the interviews, they identified a shift towards neuroscience as a new authoritative knowledge and a change in teachers’ pedagogical language.
Dr Stentiford said: “Interviewees spoke about their motivations for pursuing CPD or postgraduate neuroeducation courses, links unfolded between acquiring neuroscientific knowledge and regaining authority through certainty. They felt undertaking training in neuroscience education had represented a path to professional legitimacy.  Some were energised by neuroscience’s promise. Others criticised the marketisation of neuroscience as the source of pseudo-experts.”

A new method improving the accuracy of interpreting blood pressure measurements taken at the ankle could be crucial for people who cannot have their arm blood pressure measured.
New research from the University of Exeter Medical School, published in BMJ Open and funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), analysed data from over 33,000 people to create a personalised predictive model for more accurately estimating arm blood pressure from ankle readings – when compared to previously available methods. The team has developed an
online calculator
for healthcare professionals and patients to interpret these readings effectively.
High blood pressure affects over one billion people globally, increasing the risk of serious health issues like heart, brain, and kidney diseases. It’s therefore very important to measure and interpret blood pressure readings as accurately as possible. While blood pressure is typically measured on the arm, sometimes this is not possible due to disability, missing limbs, or problems caused by conditions such as stroke. Blood pressure can be measured at the ankle instead, but these readings are generally higher than arm values. Standard guidelines for treating blood pressure are based on arm readings only, which creates complications in making accurate estimations based on ankle measurements, potentially leading to misdiagnoses.
Professor Chris Clark from the University of Exeter Medical School led the study and said: “Our new method will give a more accurate blood pressure reading for around two percent more people. This doesn’t sound a big number but remember, around a third of adults have high blood pressure and once you get into your 60s it’s more than half of the adults. The NHS Health Check Programme diagnoses 38,000 new cases annually in England alone, so two percent equates to 750 fewer potential misdiagnoses per year in England, and tens of thousands globally.”
Researchers used statistical modelling on arm and ankle blood pressure readings from 33,710 people (mean age 58 years, 45 per cent female) across the world to help describe the relationship between arm and ankle blood pressures, predict arm blood pressure using ankle blood pressure readings, and predict important health outcomes (such as risk of heart attacks) from ankle blood pressure readings.
This research could help address a health inequality by providing accurate and personalised blood pressure measurements for people who previously could not have their blood pressure measured accurately from their arm. It’s estimated there are up to 10,000 adults currently living in the UK with upper limb loss, while 75 per cent of the country’s 1.3 million stroke survivors have upper limb dysfunction, sometimes making it difficult to measure blood pressure from their arm.
The study was supported by the Stroke Association and Thalidomide Trust.
Juliet Bouverie OBE, CEO of the Stroke Association, said: “Someone in the UK has a stroke every five minutes, with high blood pressure accounting for around half of those. Around two-thirds of stroke survivors will leave hospital with some form of disability, including paralysis in an arm, which can prevent getting accurate blood pressure readings from the affected limb. Many stroke survivors feel anxious about having another stroke, so receiving an accurate blood pressure reading in the ankle will not only provide benefits in the primary prevention of stroke, but importantly in easing the minds of stroke survivors who are already dealing with the devastating impact of stroke.”
Professor Kevin Munro, Director of NIHR’s Research for Patient Benefit Programme, said: “This research has identified an ingenious solution to an important problem – finding a way to measure blood pressure for people who cannot have it monitored via the upper arm. Keeping track of blood pressure is a vital tool to help keep people healthy and this NIHR-funded research will help to spot high blood pressure and treat it even more widely.”
The paper titled
‘Arm Based on LEg blood pressures (ABLE-BP): Can systolic ankle blood pressure measurements predict systolic arm blood pressure? An individual participant data meta-analysis from the INTERPRESS-IPD Collaboration’
is published in BMJ Open.
The online calculator is available at:
ABLE-BP Tool
“Why should I not be able to have my blood pressure taken?”
TV presenter Sue Kent, 62 from Swansea, has an upper limb disability caused by the drug Thalidomide, which was prescribed to her mother during pregnancy. She has eight-inch arms which aren’t big enough for blood pressure to be taken.
Sue said: “I rarely had my blood pressure taken when I was younger, but when I did, I used to have a really big cuff they would put around my thigh and take the blood pressure there. Whether it was accurate or not nobody worried, but I didn’t seem to have blood pressure problems.
“But then I had a cataract operation, and somebody took my blood pressure from my ankle, and it was very high. They did it three times and every time it was high, and it made me very worried. They (medical staff) weren’t worried and carried on and did the cataract operation, but I was quite distressed.”
Sue was diagnosed with Meniere’s disease in 2017, which is a rare inner ear condition which has left her partially deaf.
She said: “I was worried I was going to have a stroke because Meniere’s can be an indicator the blood flow isn’t going to the brain. I knew I couldn’t have my blood pressure taken accurately, so I went privately to have dye injected to check everything was OK.
“As you get older blood pressure is an important indicator of so many things, including things that could be seriously wrong. Prodding about in the dark and guessing isn’t really a safe thing to do. You need the right information about your blood pressure.”
Sue hopes this new method could potentially help her and thousands of others like her have something most of us take for granted – an accurate blood pressure reading.
She said: “Why should I not be able to have my blood pressure taken when it’s available to most people and is a relatively simple thing to do?
“When you’re disabled, you’re more likely to die younger for a variety of reasons, so this resource tips the scales a bit more in our favour. This could put us on a level playing field with everybody else when it comes to blood pressure. It means reassurance and maybe an early diagnosis if something is wrong.”

with hectic offensive tempo to win Game 3 of the 2025 NBA Finals on Wednesday in Indianapolis.
The Pacers, who trailed by as many as nine points in the first half, outscored the Thunder 52-47 in the second for the 116-107 triumph, giving them a 2-1 series lead and their first NBA Finals win in nearly 25 years.
"We just had guys make plays after plays," Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton, who totaled 22 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds, said on the ABC broadcast.
Bench production played a major role in Game 3, with the Pacers reserves outscoring their Thunder counterparts 49-18. The Pacers also turned the Thunders' playoff-high 19 turnovers into 21 points. Reserve wing Bennedict Mathurin scored a game-high 27 points, including 14 in the second quarter.
The Pacers (2-1) will host the Thunder (1-2) in Game 4 of the best-of-seven game series on Friday in Indianapolis.
"It's a big win for us," Haliburton said. "We are going to enjoy it. We've got a day in between. We've gotta be ready to go for Game 4."
Center Chet Holmgren dominated the Pacers with his size early on, scoring 13 points over the first 12 minutes to help the Thunder outscore their foes 32-24.
Thunder forward Luguentz Dort was 3 of 3 from 3-point range and scored nine points in the first quarter.
The Pacers started the second quarter on a 15-4 run, which included nine points from Mathurin, to take a 39-36 lead. The Thunder were 1 of 8 from the floor during that surge.
The Pacers carried that momentum into halftime for a 65-60 lead at the break. Indiana outscored the Thunder 40-28 in the second quarter.
The Thunder scored the first eight points of the second half to briefly regain momentum, but the Pacers responded with a 10-2 surge. The lead changed hands five times in the quarter. The Thunder carried an 89-84 advantage into the final frame.
The Pacers, who made just 7 of 20 shots and were 1 of 9 from 3-point range in the third quarter, started the fourth by making 6 of 8 shots. Haliburton hit a long-distance 3-pointer midway through the frame for a 101-98 advantage, which the Pacers never lost. They outscored the Thunder 18-9 over the final 6:42 to seal the win.
The Pacers outshot the Thunder 51.2% to 46.8%. Forward Pascal Siakam totaled 21 points. Veteran guard T.J. McConnell logged 10 points, five rebounds and five assists off the Pacers bench.
Gilgeous-Alexander made 9 of 20 shots en route to 24 points. Thunder forward Jalen Williams and Holmgren recorded 26 and 20 points, respectively.
Game 4 will tip off at 8:30 p.m. EDT Friday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

Islamabad: Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, accompanied by a high-level delegation, departed for the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on a one-day official visit aimed at enhancing strategic, economic, and diplomatic ties between the two brotherly nations. According to the media reports, the premier is undertaking the visit at the invitation of UAE President and Ruler of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The Pakistani delegation includes Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Ishaq Dar, Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Foreign Affairs Tariq Fatemi. During the visit, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to hold high-level meetings with the Emirati leadership. The discussions are expected to cover a wide range of bilateral, regional, and global issues of mutual interest. In a statement, the Foreign Office of Pakistan emphasized that the visit reflects the deep-rooted fraternal relationship between Pakistan and the UAE, which is based on mutual trust, shared values, and close cooperation across various sectors. The Foreign Office further noted that this visit will serve to further strengthen the time-tested brotherly relations between the two countries, deepen economic engagement, and enhance multifaceted cooperation. It also highlighted that the trip aligns with both nations shared commitment to promoting a mutually beneficial strategic partnership, exploring new avenues for collaboration, and reinforcing the warmth of their long-standing diplomatic ties. The UAE is home to a number of Pakistani expatriate population and remains a pivotal source of remittances for Pakistan. Moreover, the UAE is a key trade partner and investor, particularly in energy, real estate, and infrastructure sectors. This visit follows a series of recent diplomatic engagements by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the region. Following the rising regional tensions, particularly after recent Indian aggression, the Prime Minister has already visited Türkiye, Iran, Azerbaijan, and Tajikistan to bolster regional cooperation. Additionally, on the occasion of Eid al-Adha, he visited Saudi Arabia with Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, where they performed Umrah and held a meeting with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The outcomes of the UAE visit are expected to pave the way for enhanced bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, energy, and regional security, further reinforcing Pakistan’s diplomatic outreach in the Middle East.

In a significant strategic breakthrough, Turkey has inked its largest ever defense export deal, as 48 domestically developed KAAN fifth-generation stealth fighter jets will be supplied to Indonesia under a $10 billion agreement, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced today. The groundbreaking accord — the first international sale of the KAAN — was signed during the Indo Defence 2025 exhibition in Jakarta. President Erdoğan emphasized the collaborative nature of the deal, noting that Indonesia’s “local capabilities will also be utilized in the production of KAAN”. According to Turkish Aerospace Industries (TAI), the jets will be manufactured in Turkey but will integrate Indonesian industry contributions and local production capacity. The production timeline spans a decade, with first unit delivery of aircraft expected by 2028. As Turkey’s first homegrown fifth-generation fighter, the KAAN completed its maiden flight in February 2024. It is powered initially by proven Western engines, with locally produced TF35000 turbofan engines slated for future blocks of the program. The jets will eventually feature cutting-edge stealth enhancements, integrated air-to-air combat radar, and dual-engine supercruise performance. Valued at approximately $10 billion — a figure cited by Turkish media — the contract is one of Indonesia’s largest defense procurements to date. Indonesia benchmarks the cost at around $208 million per aircraft, positioning the KAAN as cost-competitive with existing Western options while offering stealth and modular avionics tailored to Southeast Asian defense needs. The purchase accentuates a strategic pivot in Indonesia’s defence relationships, juxtaposing its procurement of French Rafales with an embrace of non-Western aviation technology — all in the midst of the backdrop of regional security concerns in the Indo-Pacific. The experts say that the KAAN, with its stealth capabilities, drone integration, and advanced avionics, provides Jakarta a potent tool for air defense, area denial, and surveillance. For Turkey, the deal marks a milestone in its defence export ambitions. With defense exports exceeding $7.1 billion in 2024 — a $1.6 billion increase year-on-year — Turkey is now emerging as a key player in the global arms market. The KAAN represents Ankara’s entry into the elite club of nations capable of producing and exporting fifth-generation stealth fighters, alongside the US, China, and Russia. The agreement also includes significant technology transfer provisions, enabling Indonesia to develop domestic capacity and potentially contribute to future production runs or derivatives of the KAAN. Earlier in 2025, Jakarta and Ankara also agreed to collaborate on a joint Baykar combat drone factory — further deepening defense industrial cooperation. Looking ahead, the KAAN deal may pave the way for future sales to other nations, with reported interest from Qatar, Azerbaijan, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, and the UAE, who could explore a joint KAAN production venture with Turkey.

Israel’s Knesset on Thursday narrowly voted down an opposition-backed motion to dissolve the parliament, postponing the threat of early elections. The preliminary vote ended at 61–53 against the proposal, at the required threshold, where exactly the number of 61 was needed out of total 120 to annul the motion. The dissolution proposal was introduced in the midst of intense political turmoil over military conscription. The Ultra-Orthodox parties within Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition had threatened support for the motion unless their demand for continuing exemptions from compulsory service for full-time seminary students was upheld. A compromise was ultimately reached, averting a coalition collapse. Yuli Edelstein, the chair of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee, welcomed the breakthrough, stating that foundational principles for a new draft law on service obligations had been agreed upon. However, full legislation remains pending in the Knesset. The postponement relieves Netanyahu’s coalition from an immediate crisis, allowing him to delay the next general election, originally scheduled for late 2026. The right-wing government, formed in December 2022 alongside ultra-Orthodox and nationalist factions, continues to face internal dissent over military and judicial reforms. The opposition lawmaker Merav Michaeli of the Labour Party criticized Netanyahu’s administration, calling it “toxic and harmful” and arguing that early elections were urgently needed to end the Gaza war and begin national rehabilitation. Political and Security Implications The conscription issue has taken on added prominence during the over 20-month war in Gaza, which erupted after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. That attack killed approximately 1,200 Israelis and resulted in over 400 Israeli military fatalities. With the IDF under pressure from high combat losses, the conscription dispute has stirred public frustration and placed pressure on the coalition to secure more manpower. Passing this vote strengthens Netanyahu’s position, granting time to stabilize his coalition and finalize the draft legislation. However, public support for the war is reportedly dwindling following the growing concerns over rising military, social, and legal tensions. Opposition, on the other hand, has to wait at least six more months to propose a new dissolution vote against the prevailing government.

Pakistan-origin footballer Haris Zeb, who is set to participate in the FIFA Club World Cup, has expressed his willingness to represent Pakistan at the international level. Haris shared that his football journey began in childhood, playing with his cousins before moving on to school-level, club-level, and eventually top-tier football. While the sport gave him some of the best moments of his life, he also faced serious challenges along the way. Between 2021 and 2023, Haris suffered five foot injuries and underwent two surgeries, which cost him a professional opportunity in Finland. At one point, it seemed like his dream was slipping away. However, he decided to give it one last shot in 2024. His strong season with Birkenhead United brought him back into the spotlight and led to his current success. Now preparing to compete in the FIFA Club World Cup, Haris called it a great honor and a clear sign of divine planning. He confirmed that he is available to play for the Pakistan national team if selected. In the early days of his career, Haris said he faced criticism from relatives who believed football was a distraction and that he should pursue a more traditional profession, like medicine or law. However, after he started achieving success around the age of 18, those same people began to support him. Today, his family is proud of his accomplishments, and he hopes to be a role model for other Pakistani youth. Like many kids of Pakistani descent, Haris initially played cricket but never enjoyed it the way he did football. His passion for football always stood out, which is why he chose to fully commit to the sport. He described playing for Auckland City and winning the OFC Champions League as a dream come true. Representing a club at the FIFA Club World Cup is a milestone he never imagined reaching. He said this experience is a blessing and that he is determined to give his best performance. Haris reflected on the surreal feeling of playing against clubs he once only saw in FIFA video games, adding that it’s a moment he’s extremely grateful for. He also confirmed that he has been in contact with the Pakistan Football Federation and the national team coach. Although he was initially expected to attend a training camp, his current focus is on the Club World Cup. Afterward, he will be available for national duty. He emphasized that if selected, he would proudly represent Pakistan. Haris follows the progress of the Pakistan national football team closely and acknowledged the struggles the team has faced due to bans and administrative challenges. However, he sees signs of improvement and believes that with a balance of local and overseas talent, Pakistan can become a competitive force in Asia. Haris expressed deep appreciation for the support he receives from Pakistan. He said that fan messages lift his spirits and give him motivation. He hopes to give back that love through his performances and dreams of making Pakistan proud. When Haris Zeb steps onto the pitch this month for Auckland City in the FIFA Club World Cup, he will make history as the first Pakistani footballer to play in this prestigious tournament—and the first to represent Pakistan at the senior level in any FIFA world event. Though born and raised in New Zealand, Haris Zeb’s roots trace back to Pakistan. He carries a strong connection to his heritage and is eager to contribute to the rise of football in the country.

Pakistani actress Naeema Butt, known for her prominent role in last year’s popular drama Kabhi Main, Kabhi Tum, recently shared an emotional message on Instagram, hinting at heartbreak and spiritual healing. In a cryptic Instagram story, Naeema referred to a mysterious person identified only as “J,” and expressed her pain and reflections on relationships. She wrote, “With time, you realize that almost all relationships are the same. It’s better to be alone than to be left by someone — but then why don’t we choose to stay alone?” She further added that the best source of peace is connecting with Allah (SWT), stating, “That’s it, and that’s enough. But J… I still miss you.” In a previous interview, Naeema Butt had revealed that someone very special had once been a part of her life — a person she deeply loved. However, she shared that he is no longer in this world. Since his passing, she said, external beauty or the desire to love someone again no longer holds any meaning for her. The actress’s emotional post has left fans speculating about the identity of “J” while many continue to offer her support and prayers during this difficult time. Earlier, Actress Naeema Butt, who became popular for her strong performance as Rubab in the hit drama Kabhi Main Kabhi Tum, recently spoke about the reality of fake relationships in showbiz on her visit to a talk show. Speaking from her own experience, Naeema was dismayed at the way individuals in the business world tend to be fake friends on social media. “I have seen that most people pretend to be close friends on Instagram, but they are not the same in real life as they present themselves on social media,” she stated. Referring to her co-stars of Kabhi Main Kabhi Tum, she let on, “They gave it the impression on social media that we were really close, but they did everything else but. There were even instances during public functions when they tried to usher me off the stage.”

In a recent development in Lahore, Salman Haider, a co-accused in a case involving alleged sexual assault by TikTok influencer Rajab Butt, was granted interim bail by the Additional Sessions Judge Syed Najaf Haider. The court has restrained the police from arresting him until June 18, 2025, and directed him to cooperate with the investigation. The police have been ordered to present a progress report at the next hearing. The case stems from allegations made by a female TikTok creator who accused Rajab Butt and five others, including Salman Haider, of sexual assault. The complaint was filed at the Nawab Town police station, and the investigation is ongoing. This case adds to the legal challenges faced by Rajab Butt, who has been involved in multiple legal matters. Notably, he was granted protective bail in January 2025 by the Lahore High Court in a blasphemy case registered against him in Karachi. The court allowed him to approach the relevant court in Karachi before the next hearing. in further news, Lahore Sessions Court has granted interim bail to YouTuber Rajab Butt in a case registered against him under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) and Section 295-C of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). The court has directed the police to refrain from arresting him until June 21, 2025, and has ordered him to cooperate with the investigation. Rajab Butt appeared in court and completed his attendance. The case was filed at Nishtar Colony Police Station, and the investigation is ongoing. The court’s decision reflects the legal process in Pakistan, where bail is granted at the discretion of the court, considering factors such as the nature of the offense and the accused’s cooperation with the investigation. This development adds to the legal challenges faced by Rajab Butt, who has been involved in multiple controversies. Notably, he was granted post-arrest bail in December 2024 after being detained for possessing a lion cub and unlicensed weapons. He was sentenced to community service for keeping the lion cub and was ordered to produce monthly vlogs discussing animal rights

Love erased borders and social media brought two hearts together. In a heartwarming story, a 27-year-old American woman traveled to Jhang, Pakistan, to marry her social media friend after embracing Islam. Karensha Madison Grace, a resident of South Carolina, USA, tied the knot with 29-year-old Naeem-ul-Hassan from Jhang. The two had been in contact through social media for the past two years, and their online friendship gradually blossomed into love. Motivated by her feelings, Karensha journeyed to Pakistan and accepted Islam at Jamia Arabia Dar-ul-Huda in Jhang, where she adopted the Islamic name Kaneez Ayesha. Later, the couple was officially married in the presence of witnesses. Speaking to the media after the nikah ceremony, Kaneez Ayesha said she came to Pakistan out of love for Naeem-ul-Hassan and has decided to settle here permanently. She revealed that she was previously married in the U.S. and is a mother of three children. However, she clarified that she had legally divorced her former husband before entering into a relationship with Naeem. It’s worth noting that a similar case occurred recently when 33-year-old American woman Oneja Andrew Robinson came to Karachi to marry her 19-year-old social media friend. However, that marriage did not materialize, and she eventually returned to the United States. New York woman Onijah Andrew Robinson made headlines in Pakistan and India as a viral celebrity after she had gone to Karachi to meet her purported online boyfriend, 19-year-old Nidal Ahmed Memon of Garden East, Karachi. Onijah landed in Pakistan on October 11, 2024, saying that she had fallen in love with Nidal after meeting online. She later, however, reported that both Nidal and his family declined to meet her upon arrival. Despite the fact that her 30-day visa had expired, Onijah remained in Karachi. While addressing a press conference, she drew more media attention by asking to be compensated millions of dollars per week. In February 2025, Onijah was formally deported from Pakistan. Now, for the first time since the incident, Nidal Ahmed has revealed in a YouTube interview what happened.

Dr. Mahrang Baloch, a prominent leader of the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), is currently detained in Quetta’s Hudda District Jail under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) law. Her sister, Nadia Baloch, has filed a petition in the Supreme Court of Pakistan, challenging her ongoing detention and seeking relief. The petition urges the Supreme Court to overturn the Balochistan High Court’s April 15 decision, which had dismissed Dr. Mahrang’s initial plea against her arrest. She was taken into custody on March 22 following an order by the Deputy Commissioner of Quetta issued under the MPO. Filed through senior lawyer Faisal Siddiqui, the appeal argues that the High Court’s judgment contradicts the Constitution, applicable legal standards, and the facts of the case. It claims that Dr. Mahrang’s repeated arrests and accusations of being sympathetic to militants are part of an orchestrated effort to silence her activism, particularly her advocacy for missing persons in Balochistan. The federal government, the Ministry of Interior, the Balochistan Home Department, the Prosecutor General, the Inspector General of Police, the Director General of the FIA, and the Deputy Commissioner of Quetta have all been named as respondents in the case. The appeal also informs the court that Dr. Mahrang’s father and brother were victims of enforced disappearances in 2011 and 2017 respectively, which further fuels her commitment to raising awareness about such issues. An additional application has been submitted requesting a suspension of the High Court’s ruling until the Supreme Court delivers its final verdict. Another petition is expected soon to challenge the extension of her detention order. The appeal notes that the December 2023 Baloch Long March, led by Dr. Mahrang and other BYC members, was met with alleged excessive force by state authorities. It also highlights a rise in state actions after a militant attack on a passenger train on March 11. According to the petition, on March 20, BYC member Beebarg Zehri and his brother were abducted from their home, while on March 19, another relative, Saeeda Baloch, was detained for two days without charge. The petition argues that the High Court failed to demand and review all necessary evidence that justified the application of the MPO. It insists that had the full record been presented, the court could have evaluated whether the detention order was reasonable and lawful. It cites a 2003 Supreme Court ruling, which holds that authorities must present all relevant material—even if claimed confidential—for the court’s assessment when a person’s liberty is at stake under public order laws. The appeal concludes by stating that denying interim relief would result in irreparable harm and that the Deputy Commissioner’s order lacked legal authority, as it was issued without the Chief Minister’s approval and in a unilateral manner.

Dr. Mahrang Baloch’s sister challenges her deten...

You don't need a gaming mouse. You probably just need practice. Just pick a game that you like to play.
The two things that are most likely to help are 1) turn off mouse acceleration/smoothing in the game you're playing and 2) turn the sensitivity down. You want to make your reticle movements, predictable, and repeatable. Disabling mouse acceleration makes it so that every time you move the mouse a given distance, your reticle will always move a fixed distance. If acceleration is on then moving your mouse at different speeds will move the reticle different distances.

most people's mouse sensitivities are way, way too high for proper aim (not that it's impossible, but it's probably not worth working through it)

sens converter to find your cm/360
you don't necessarily need new gear just yet, but it'll help; everyday mousepads have neither the surface nor the size you want in the long run, and office mouse sensors and weight over 60 grams or so are both hindrances
neither one requires breaking the bank; there are very good mousepads on sale frequently and there are far better Chinese mice on the market that destroy the ubiquitous mainstream G Pro Superlight and Razer offerings
if you want to improve with higher efficiency for your time spent, don't grind your game of choice exclusively and add some aim trainer routines instead; AimLabs is free to play if you don't want to spend $5 on Kovaaks just yet

1. Turn off Mouse acceleration and smoothing.
2. Lower the mouse sensitivity.
3. Get a bigger mouse pad or surface you use for your mouse. When all is said in done you should be able to consistently do figure eights with your mouse cursor with some degree of consistency.
4. Aim with your wrist/Hand as opposed to your full arm. Some might say the opposite but this part is what I'd consider subjective.

I would say...
1) Start with a low mouse sensitivity.
2) Disable mouse acceleration (or anything that implies mouse movement won't be 1:1).
3) Always be aiming. If you're playing a shooter it's not a case of just trying to snap-aim at every target. Your reticle should be (at least while adapting) consciously hovering over targets / 'points of interest'. One exercise could be to try 'locking' your aim to a corner while you strafe. Point being it's not just something to practice in moments of action.

When a
manicure trend
coined "Italian
summer nails
" began to pop off on my feed, it felt less like a passing beauty moment and more like a personal summons. I'm Italian—like grew-up-on-carbonara-and-Sunday-dinners Italian—so much so, that my parents named me after a city in
Tuscany
. (No, for real,
Siena,
if you missed the byline.) So yeah, this trend? It literally had my name written all over it.
Depending on which side of social media you land on, Italian
summer nails
can go one of two ways. On one end, there's the fun, warm weather, Mediterranean side: Amalfi lemons, Venetian sardines, and colors practically pulled straight from a Capri postcard. It's curated for the very aesthetic that comes with the term
Euro summer
.
Then there's the other take on the trend—the one that feels straight out of a
Sopranos
episode: square
French tips
(à la Carmela),
cherry reds
, and bling-galore. A manicure that wouldn't look out of place accompanied by a
stack of gold rings
and over-the-top expressive hand gestures. This side once felt flashy, but now takes on a deeply feminine, cool-girl vibe as
mob wife
core reignites its flame this summer.
So in the name of research (and my personal interests), I did a deep dive: I texted the cousins, tapped nail artist and
Après Nail
Educator,
Priscilla Nguyen
, and rounded up the products and polish shades you need to pull it off without actually booking a flight, below.

Pakistani singer Asim Azhar has announced the end of his three-year engagement with actress and model Meerub Ali, leaving fans surprised and disappointed. The couple, who once seemed deeply in love, have now parted ways, adding their names to the long list of showbiz breakups. Before Meerub, Asim Azhar was known for his relationship with actress Hania Aamir. The two were often seen together at events and on social media in 2019, sparking widespread attention. However, their relationship ended in a highly publicized breakup, during which Asim faced significant online trolling. In the midst of that, on March 20, 2022, he unexpectedly announced his engagement to Meerub Ali through a joint social media post, surprising his fans. While many fans were happy about the engagement, it also stirred controversy. Meerub had previously been friends with Hania Aamir, which led to speculation and criticism when she became romantically involved with Asim following his breakup with Hania. This shift in dynamics led to ongoing gossip and public interest in the trio’s relationships. A few months ago, Asim hinted at the possibility of getting married in 2025, raising hopes among fans. However, he recently shared a heartfelt message on Instagram confirming that he and Meerub had decided to go their separate ways. In his statement, Asim wrote that after much thought and consideration, they had chosen to end their relationship. He acknowledged the beautiful moments they had shared and the dreams they once held, but said that life sometimes takes its own path. He emphasized that both he and Meerub continue to hold deep respect for one another and for their families. He also requested that people respect their privacy during this time and treat the matter with the same dignity as when the relationship was first announced. Asim expressed gratitude for the love and support from fans throughout the journey. Although the message used the word “we,” the post was shared only by Asim Azhar. Meerub Ali has not commented or posted anything on her own social media. The two have unfollowed each other on Instagram and removed their pictures together, signaling a complete end to their relationship. Fans, meanwhile, have expressed sadness and are eager to understand the reasons behind the sudden breakup.
The post
Asim Azhar & Meerub Ali call off engagement
appeared first on
Minute Mirror
.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has officially taken note of the significant salary increases recently approved for some of the country’s highest-ranking parliamentary figures, including the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Senate, as well as the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. According to insider sources, the Prime Minister has expressed concern over the timing and scale of these salary enhancements, especially as the general public and civil servants are grappling with inflation and economic difficulties. He has formally requested a comprehensive report on the matter from both the Speaker of the National Assembly and the Chairman of the Senate. This report is expected to provide a detailed justification for the salary increments and outline the process through which these changes were approved. Once the report is submitted, the Prime Minister will carefully examine its findings and make a final decision on whether the increases will be upheld, modified, or possibly reversed. His intervention reflects growing public criticism and debate regarding the appropriateness of such raises at a time when the majority of the population is facing economic hardship. The controversy emerged shortly after the federal budget for the upcoming fiscal year was announced. The budget proposed a 10 percent raise in salaries for general government employees and a 7 percent increase in pensions. While these adjustments were modest, the substantial rise in the remuneration packages of the top parliamentary figures has sparked widespread backlash. During the post-budget press conference held yesterday, a representative from Geo News questioned the Finance Minister about the logic behind granting significant raises to ministers, parliamentarians, and key parliamentary officeholders. In response, the Finance Minister justified the decision, stating that their salaries had remained stagnant since 2016 and were overdue for revision. He emphasized that the increase was meant to adjust for inflation and the rising cost of living. Despite this defense, criticism continues to mount. In a strongly worded statement posted on social media, Defense Minister Khawaja Asif voiced his disapproval, labeling the raises as a form of “financial obscenity.” He pointed out the contradiction in offering such financial incentives to top officials while millions of ordinary citizens struggle to make ends meet. The Prime Minister’s decision to take notice suggests a recognition of the sensitive nature of the issue and its political implications. As the country navigates through economic challenges, the scrutiny of governmental spending — particularly on high-ranking officials — is likely to intensify.

appeared first on

.

Pentagon Is Reviewing Deal to Equip Australia With Nuclear Submarines
https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/11/world/asia/australia-nuclear-submarines-trump.html
The first bit of good news is that the Pentagon is reviewing the decision to sell nuclear attack submarines to Australia. This does not necessarily mean it is going to cancel the deal, because it is normal for a new administration to review previous military deals.
The Trump administration is reviewing whether a deal to equip Australia with nuclear submarines is "aligned with the president's America First agenda," sowing doubt on the future of the
landmark agreement
between the United States, Britain and Australia, which is meant to counter China's rise in the Asia Pacific.
News of the Pentagon's review of the security pact dominated headlines on Thursday in Australia, which has made the deal the centerpiece of its defense in the coming decades and has already invested heavily in the industrial base and training needed to maintain and build the submarines.

Under the agreement, Australia is scheduled to
receive
used
Virginia-class nuclear submarines
from the United States in the 2030s while scaling up the capacity to build its own, using a British design. But there has been concern in both Washington and Canberra about whether the United States can build new submarines to replenish its fleet quickly enough for the older ones to be given to Australia.
In January, Australia transferred $500 million to the United States, the first in what is supposed to be $3 billion in payments to boost the U.S. submarine industry.
Elbridge Colby, the U.S. under secretary of defense for policy, said during his Senate confirmation hearing in March that he was skeptical about the pragmatic feasibility of the Aukus deal. Mr. Colby is now in charge of the Pentagon's review of the pact, according to The Financial Times.
"If we can produce the attack submarines in sufficient number and sufficient speed, then great," Mr. Colby
said

E-2 Hawkeye Replaces USAF E-3 Sentry, E-7 Cancelled In New Budget
E-2 Hawkeye Replaces USAF E-3 Sentry, E-7 Cancelled In New Budget
The E-2D is far smaller than the E-7 and lacks some of its abilities, but it can fly from austere forward bases where the E-7 cannot.
www.twz.com
The second bit of good news is that the USAF is retiring the 4 decade old E-3 aerial early warning systems and cancelling the expensive E-7 that was meant to replace the E-3. It is instead going to buy the much smaller E-2 as a stopgap while it deploys space-based detection systems.
A seismic shift has occurred in the Trump administration's new defense spending plan that is just emerging when it comes to the USAF's airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) predicament. The service's
E-3 Sentry
Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft are
dwindling in number and rapidly aging
into unsupportability. The proven and in-production
E-7 Wedgetail
, based on the Boeing 737 and serving with multiple allies, was supposed to bridge the gap between the E-3's retirement and pushing the sending part of the mission to space-based distributed satellite constellations. You can read all about this
here
. Now, if the administration gets its wish, that won't happen. The E-7 will be cancelled and the E-2D Hawkeye, currently flown by the U.S. Navy, will step in to fill the gap.
This major turn of events came to light today as Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U.S. Air Force Gen. John Caine, and Bryn Woollacott MacDonnell testified before the Senate Appropriations Committee. MacDonnell is Special Assistant to the Secretary of Defense and is currently performing the duties of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) and the Pentagon's Chief Financial Officer. In 2023, the USAF announced its intention to
purchase E-7s, potentially as many as 26
of them, as replacements for a portion of the E-3 fleet.
Click to expand...
Click to shrink...
"The answer is yes. I would. I would file this entire discussion under difficult choices that we have to make. But you know, the E-7, in particular, is sort of late, more expensive and 'gold plated,' and so filling the gap, and then shifting to space-based ISR [intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance] is a portion of how we think we can do it best, considering all the challenges," Hegseth responded.
At a separate hearing before the House Appropriations Committee yesterday, Hegsteth had also described the Wedgetail as an example of a capability that is "not survivable in the modern battlefield" and mentioned broad plans "to fund existing platforms that are there more robustly and make sure they're modernized."
Click to expand...
Click to shrink...
Above all else, there are major capability trades here. The Hawkeye is a much smaller aircraft than both the Sentry and the Wedgetail. It is extremely capable, but it is also optimized to exist within the confines of carrier operations. The crew size is just five individuals. This limits the amount of shear manpower to perform highly complex operations and other tasks beyond traditional AEW&C.
The E-2 also has less range and is far slower than both the E-3 and E-7. This means longer transit times, and the aircraft doesn't fit in as seamlessly with the jet-centric operations for the counter-air mission the service currently enjoys. The E-2D's AN/APY-9 radar from Lockheed Martin is hugely capable, but many of its other advanced data fusion and relay systems are unique to the Navy. These systems would either be stripped or just left unused for USAF-focused operations. It's also possible that other systems will replace them, but this will cost money and take time to integrate and field.
Hawkeyes, being turboprop aircraft, also operate at lower altitudes, giving their radar, radio systems, and electronic surveillance suites reduced line-of-sight, limiting their range and fidelity at distance for some targets and surveillance application, in some cases.

The U.S. Navy's future
Constellation
class frigates are set to be at least 759 metric tons (close to 867 U.S. tons) heavier than expected, a 13 percent increase over earlier estimates. Concerns have
previously been raised about how weight growth

The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), a Congressional watchdog, included the new details about the
Constellation

an annual assessment of major procurement efforts
across the U.S. military released today. The U.S. Navy chose Marinette Marine in Wisconsin, a wholly owned subsidiary of Italy's Fincantieri, to build the new frigates in 2020. The ship's core design is derived from the

It is unclear from the GAO report whether this 759 metric ton increase is in terms of gross weight or displacement, and whether or not it is a total figure or additive on top of previous growth. By 2021,

As both countries prepare for another round of nuclear negotiations, Iran Defence Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh made it clear that Iran will defend itself if provoked. He said that if the US decides to impose conflict instead of a peaceful agreement, all American bases in the region are within Iran’s reach and will be targeted if needed. This is not a threat, but a clear message of self-defence. The US, especially under President Donald Trump, has often used the language of pressure and threats against Iran. Trump has warned of bombing Iran if it does not accept a deal on America’s terms. This bullying approach goes against the spirit of diplomacy and mutual respect. Talks between Iran and the US are expected to resume soon, with both sides offering proposals for a new nuclear agreement. However, the US continues to push Iran to make unfair compromises, especially on issues like uranium enrichment and missile development. Iran has always said its nuclear program is for peaceful purposes—like producing energy and medicine—not for making weapons. Despite this, the US and some Western countries continue to accuse Iran without proof. Iran Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi shared a hopeful message, saying that a fair and peaceful agreement is possible and could happen quickly—if both sides act respectfully and honestly. But Iran has made it clear that it will not accept restrictions on its missile program, which it sees as a vital part of its defence. Recently, Iran successfully tested a missile with a two-ton warhead, showing its military strength and technological progress. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has also said that Iran must continue strengthening its military to protect its people and sovereignty. In short, Iran is seeking peace—but not at the cost of its dignity and security.

Preface - A brief history summary
Hi, I'd like to preface that while the use of gaming on a MacOS device is very niche and marginal in the wider gaming space. With the switch to
Apple Silicon
(AS), Apple has switched to an ARM architecture for all their laptop, desktop devices. Thus completely unifying a architecture that goes from bottom (iPhone) to top (Mac Pro). With that switch, the entry level devices (Mac mini & Macbook Air) now have more capable internal GPUs (iGPU) compared to the x86 intel-based devices, whose internal GPUs were not capable of running any of games that were available in that time period. This left your only option to go for a device with a discrete GPUs, which were a lot higher in pricing, making it nonsensical for any
secondary
gaming purpose. Moreover, you'd often be better off playing games through Bootcamp, that allowed you to install windows next to MacOS, which provided not much incentive for developers to release games native on MacOS as you'd have some option. However you're left at the mercy of the OEM (& apple) providing continuous driver support.
Metal, which is the proprietary graphics API that apple uses on their OS and mobile devices, also wasn't as ripe for supporting the features developers may require for full compatibility and only few ports (e.g. by Feral Interactive) were brought out. That process of porting can be cost/work intensive. In addition the removal of 32-bit support also made quite a large chunk of legacy applications & games incompatible (2019), as not all developers can continuously allocate resources to upkeep the small segment of the gaming demographic and with no bootcamp on ARM silicon, you were left with the small selection of 64-bit games that were left on MacOS when the transition to AS (ARM) started (2020). Thus iPhone has been (and still is) the primary target for any gaming purpose for Apple, especially with the focus on Apple Arcade. However!
As we're entering the third iteration of apple's ARM processors, there's been quite some change in this space. In 2023 alone, we've seen the announcement and releases of 13 titles from either small or large gaming studios. Now that's not a lot of course, but in WWDC23 the release of Apple's Game Porting Toolkit, which is a porting tool for developers to ease the time spent on getting a game up and running on MacOS and focus on profiling of cutbacks needed to run the game and spent resources on the porting process alone. Thus bringing a "console-like" developer focus to the platform. However, Apple released this tool freely for all Apple developers, which homebrew devs are using it like a proton-layer, familiar for those on linux, allowing you to play most (64-bit) DX11/DX12 without the hassle of going through
many
loopholes of getting it up an running. Performance may not always be ideal, but hey that hasn't been the case for most of the time!
Now you may be thinking, aren't you hyping it a bit too much? No one's really buying an Apple device
for
gaming and I'd agree with that. The way I see it; "I have a mac and I'd like to game on it, but I'm not buying it for gaming" is the motivation -> a secondary purpose for your device. These devices are not always the cheapest and may cost an arm & leg ;), and the majority of buyers are likely owning a macbook (pro) for all their portable computing needs, after that mac mini & iMac. Thus looping back to the start of the story, AS is quite potent and gaming on it is more feasible and we'll see overtime if it's going to stay or not. I'm an enthusiast user and it would be nice for it to grow more as a platform on which I can play my games on also without resorting to multiple devices.
So, in this first post I'll give you an brief overview of where to get the games, some resources of how it can perform and perhaps share some of our own. I don't expect many to be in this OT, but it would be nice if we can make a little community for ourselves :).

Rosetta2
This section concerns the large amount of x86 MacOS applications and games that are runnable due to the availability of the Rosetta2, which is a binary dynamic translator. Essentially what it means that 64-bit applications (remember the intel flag above?) will run through this translation layer, in layman description, your AS processor will pretend that it's an intel CPU. This has
some
impact on the performance, but it's relatively marginal. Rosetta2 does not support instruction sets such as AVX, AVX2, which will mean that some applications can not run despite being 64-bit, but w.r.t. gaming on MacOS this will not be a big concern.
The detailed description is provided here;
https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/security/secebb113be1/web
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment
You'll automatically be prompted to install Rosetta 2 as soon as you open an x86_64 application.

Virtualisation
Virtualization software concerns running a complete windows OS (or Linux distro) installation through a virtual machine on-top of MacOS. However virtualization software is licensed and often limit the RAM and cores you could run your games on. Thus potentionally inhibiting performance on heavy games. UTM does not currently support GPU emulation/virtualization on Windows and therefore lacks support for 3D acceleration (e.g. OpenGL and DirectX). You may be able to run older games with software rendering options, but nothing with hardware acceleration.
In general, you'll run the game code natively through window's WOW64 layer, which could result in less compatibility issues compared to Wine. Explanation of this layer is as following,
as per the documentation
;
The WOW64 layer of Windows allows x86 code to run on the Arm64 version of Windows. x86 emulation works by compiling blocks of x86 instructions into Arm64 instructions with optimizations to improve performance. A service caches these translated blocks of code to reduce the overhead of instruction translation and allow for optimization when the code runs again. The caches are produced for each module so that other apps can make use of them on first launch.

I Demoed Pragmata, Capcom's Upcoming Space Shooter, and It's Unlike Anything I've Played
Pragmata emerged from its five-year slumber at Summer Game Fest to wow me with its unique blend of shooter and puzzle gameplay.
By
Zackery Cuevas
Zackery Cuevas
Analyst, Hardware
My Experience
I’m an Analyst and ISF-certified TV calibrator focused on reviewing computer accessories, laptops, gaming monitors, and video games. I’ve been writing, playing, and complaining about games for as long as I remember, but it wasn’t until recently that I’ve been able to shout my opinions directly at a larger audience. My work has appeared on iMore, Windows Central, Android Central, and TWICE, and I have a diverse portfolio of editing work under my belt from my time spent at Scholastic and Oxford University Press. I also have a few book-author credits under my belt—I’ve contributed to the sci-fi anthology
Under New Suns,
and I’ve even written a Peppa Pig book.

(Credit: Capcom)
Pragmata's been M.I.A. for a long time. Announced during a PlayStation 5 showcase way back in 2020, Capcom's mysterious new space title has been cooking for nearly six years. After a long gestation period, the sci-fi shooter reemerged at the Summer Game Fest alongside
Onimusha: Way of the Sword
and
Resident Evil Requiem
. Capcom invited me to play a Pragmata demo, and the upcoming game isn't what I expected. For the most part, that's a good thing.
Gameplay: Hack and Shoot to Victory
The demo opened in what appeared to be an abandoned cargo bay on a spaceship. I controlled a wounded astronaut, Hugh, who's patched up by an android, Diana, who resembles a little girl. The demo wasted no time on exposition, as I soon faced a heavily armored, robotic enemy that was virtually impervious to damage. It's here that Pragmata unveiled its unique gameplay loop: You must use Diana to successfully hack the robot before Hugh can do significant damage with his gun.
Capcom ups the challenge by making you hack foes in real time. Diana, riding on Hugh's back, automatically initiates a hack when you aim the gun at an enemy. While locked onto a robot, you use the controller's face buttons to quickly navigate a Snake-like puzzle. The hack is successful when you connect with the green node at the end of the puzzle. This cracks the robot's armor, revealing the glowing, vulnerable bits within.
There are other nodes to consider besides the green one. Passing through the puzzle's blue node boosted my damage output if I did so before completing the hack.
It took some time to get used to the control scheme. At first, it was difficult to stay aware of the enemy's placement
and
avoid getting hit while navigating the hacking puzzle. This gets especially tricky when dealing with multiple foes at one time. It's like tapping your head and rubbing your stomach, except in this case, you're dodging projectiles shot from killer robots.
(Credit: Capcom)
I was surprised by how much Pragmata reminded me of
Dead Space
in design, though Pragmata is a largely bloodless affair. But as I engaged more enemies, Pragmata started to feel more like
Bayonetta
, a game I love because of its fast-paced action. Once you get used to the odd gameplay premise, hacking while dodging feels really good, and more arcade-like than I expected.

Hacking is not just for combat, though. As I moved through the space station, I was tasked with hacking five nodes to open a door. Hacking the environment is as simple as aiming at the hackable object and clearing a quick minigame. They were simple challenges.
(Credit: Capcom)
Environments and Other Weapons
Exploring the space station gave me a few minutes to admire the stark white walls and ceilings, and the inky black space just outside. The ship's AI, IDUS, remained operational. I didn't interact with IDUS much, but it immediately reminded me of Hal 9000 from
2001: A Space Odyssey
.
Recommended by Our Editors
First Look at Resident Evil Requiem, Capcom's Gore-Soaked Nightmare
I Got a Closed-Door Demo of the Upcoming Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Its Parry-Heavy Action Looks Fantastic
Who Needs Resident Evil 9? Indie Games Stole the Show at Summer Game Fest 2025
Hacking and shooting would quickly grow dull if there weren't enough gameplay variety. Fortunately, I found two cool weapons. The first was the Shockwave Gun, which resembled a shotgun. The other was a Stasis Net that produced a net that stunned enemies in place. This is when Pragmata fully clicked with me. Stunning robots, quickly hacking them, and then letting off with the shotgun felt
good
.
My only concern is that navigating the space station isn't nearly as engaging as the combat. I won't give Pragmata too much grief at this point in development, of course, as it's still got some more time to flesh out its ideas.
Platforms and Release Date
I wasn't sure what to expect when I went in to play Pragmata, but I walked out of the demo session with a better sense of what's to come. The hack-and-shoot gameplay, despite its learning curve, feels excellent once you get your head around it. I can't wait to see more of this game. Pragmata is scheduled to release on the PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series in 2026.

Disney, Universal Sue Midjourney for Creating 'Bottomless Pit of Plagiarism'
The studios, which own Marvel, Lucasfilm, and DreamWorks content, describe Midjourney as 'a virtual vending machine' that spits out near copies of their characters.
By
Rob Pegoraro
June 11, 2025
Threads
Bluesky
Flipboard
Copied
Error!
Copy Link
https://www.pcmag.com/news/disney-universal-sue-midjourney-for-creating-bottomless-pit-of-plagiarism
Email
Comments
(Credit: Rob Pegoraro/Midjourney)
A new hazard has materialized in Midjourney’s path: a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Universal on Wednesday that accuses the
AI image-generation
platform of duplicating the copyrighted work of the two entertainment giants.
In the suit, Disney's studios—Disney Enterprises, Marvel Characters, MVL Film Finance, Lucasfilm Ltd., and Twentieth Century Fox Film—as well as Universal’s Universal City Studios Productions and DreamWorks Animation describe
Midjourney
as "a virtual vending machine" that spits out near copies of their characters.
The
110-page complaint
alleges that the Bay Area startup first engaged in extensive
scraping
of the studios’ content to train its algorithms, allowing Midjourney to generate impressively accurate renditions of such Disney and Universal characters as Darth Vader, Bart Simpson, Iron Man, and Shrek, even in response to generic prompts like "popular 90’s animated cartoon with yellow skin."
(The extensive screengrabs showing Midjourney’s output next to Disney and Universal still images make this the most colorful legal filing we have seen yet.)
“By helping itself to Plaintiffs’ copyrighted works, and then distributing images (and soon videos) that blatantly incorporate and copy Disney’s and Universal’s famous characters—without investing a penny in their creation—Midjourney is the quintessential copyright free-rider and a bottomless pit of plagiarism,” the complaint reads.
Disney and Universal cite a
January 2024 piece in IEEE Spectrum
by Gary Marcus and Reid Southen about “plagiaristic outputs” from generative-AI systems, as well as 2022 interviews of Midjourney CEO David Holz by
Forbes
and
The Verge
in which he described an indiscriminate scraping process that ignored copyright considerations.
Under copyright law, a fictional character itself, not just the creative work in which it appears, is entitled to legal protection until
it enters the public domain
, a point that is
decades away
for the cast covered in the Disney-Universal suit.
The complaint contrasts Midjourney’s prolific creation of lookalike images of Disney and Universal characters with the service’s enforcement of provisions banning nudity and
images of political candidates
. And it says that aside from one acknowledgment of a cease-and-desist letter from Disney’s legal counsel, Midjourney did not respond to the studios before they sued.

Disney and Universal’s suit ends with an open-ended request for damages, the restitution of Midjourney’s profits, and an injunction permanently barring the company from copying or recreating the studios’ content.
Midjourney did not immediately respond to a Wednesday request for comment.
Reframing the AI Copyright Argument
The service offers a variety of subscription plans, starting at a “Basic” offering at $10 a month or $96 a year. It debuted in 2022 as a service hosted on a
Discord
server and quickly drew interest
among creative types
intrigued by the possibilities of generative AI; last year, Midjourney
opened direct access on its own site
.
Recommended by Our Editors
Why We're Suing OpenAI
1,000 AI-Enhanced Works Now Protected by US Copyright Law
How to Use Midjourney to Create High-Quality AI-Generated Images
From the get-go, “gen AI” has
raised ethical questions
about both how AI platforms must ingest vast volumes of copyrighted work and how closely their output can duplicate those originals.
“The supply chain for generative AI technology implicates a number of novel and complex questions of copyright law, particularly around fair use, whose answers are hard to predict in advance,” emailed
Blake Reid
, a professor at the University of Colorado Law School.
“But this complaint’s rhetoric and dozens of pages of generative AI outputs juxtaposed with familiar characters strike me as an effort to reframe the issues in much simpler terms"—a straightforward case of plagiarism, Blake says.
Some
lawsuits
about gen AI have already been making their way through the courts. In February, a federal judge ruled for Thomson Reuters in holding that an AI service’s copying of content from that company’s Westlaw platform
did not constitute “fair use” under copyright law
. In March, another judge allowed a copyright-infringement suit brought against Meta by a group of authors, including Sarah Silverman and Ta-Nehisi Coates
to proceed
.
PCMag’s parent company Ziff Davis is among the publishers pursuing litigation against AI platforms, having
filed a lawsuit against OpenAI
in April 2025 alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

Rob Pegoraro writes about interesting problems and possibilities in computers, gadgets, apps, services, telecom, and other things that beep or blink. content:
The finance minister is talking at length about the budget and its many aspects but not as much about the pension reforms undertaken by the government. The most important part of the pension reforms is limiting family pension facility to 10 years. For many this has come as a shock. Many beneficiaries are confused and perplexed and also scared. Majority of the beneficiaries are women, who are either divorced, unmarried or single, and whose only source of income is their parents’ pension. By restricting the family pension to just a decade, the government would be depriving thousands of women of their only source of income. This proposal therefore should be reconsidered on humanitarian basis. The government can implement any kind of reform but should spare the family pension family. It would be cruelty on the part of the government if it went ahead and implemented the family pension period restriction. Therefore through this editorial, the governments in the Centre and all provinces are requested to continue extending the family pension facility and not limit it to a certain period. Now back to other aspects in the proposed budget. The Pakistan Stock Exchange opened on a positive note, gaining over 2,000 points, with the KSE-100 index crossing the 124,000 mark following the announcement of the budget. As in the words of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the bullish run was the sign of the investors’ confidence in the government’s policies and approval of the federal budget. However there are some businessmen who are not very optimistic about it, calling it a ‘camouflage’ budget. In his post-budget press briefing, Finance Minister Mohammad Aurangzeb interacted with mediapersons and elaborated on various points of the federal budget. The minister emphasized on tariff reforms, saying reduction in import duties was the key to export-led economy. He talked about the relief provided to the salaried class in the budget, saying that the tax burden on them had been reduced while government employees were given a 10 per cent raise in salaries and seven per cent increase in pensions. He further said that this raise had been given keeping in mind the prevailing level of inflation. However the minister stressed the need to benchmark salaries and pensions with inflation. He also spoke about steps taken in the real estate, agriculture and construction sectors, with all three given some form of relief.
The post
Please do not restrict family pension period
appeared first on
Minute Mirror
.
